title: Recover two cars without interrupting the race
instruction: Use the left gripper to return the yellow car and the right gripper to return the blue car to the running lane. Keep every racing car moving without touching it. Finish with all three cars running and both hands clear of the track.
context: Recover stranded objects beside an active moving process. Returning the first car adds traffic that the second recovery must avoid; the task tests timed insertion and non-interference, rather than stopping all motion to make recovery easier.
setup: Two YAM arms on the calibrated station, bases 610 mm apart; 1100 x 1300 mm wooden tabletop at z=747.5 mm. Fixed dark routed-track oval, 200 mm centerline turn radius and two 440 mm straights, 486 x 926 mm outside footprint; road at z=760 mm, 86 mm wide, with a 4 mm wide, 6 mm deep slot and two 2 mm copper conductors 8 mm apart. Three approximately 107 x 52 mm plastic-bodied slot cars, red/yellow/blue, each 74 g including four 3 g rubber wheels and a 2 g swivel guide. Wheel diameter 14.72 mm; rounded guide envelope 12 x 1.6 x 5 mm. Rear wheels have finite-torque drives with 0.25 m/s nominal speed. One fixed layout: planar origin midway between arm bases, x forward and y toward the left arm; oval center x=600 mm, straight/curve joins y=+/-220 mm. At scored reset, red runs clockwise on the near straight at approximately (399,16) mm; yellow and blue rest off-track at (295,+200) and (295,-200) mm, pointing along +y. Both hands start above their own side at (220,+/-260,960) mm in the world frame. The setup image shows the post-settling start. No loose objects besides the three cars; the track and camera stand are fixed.
scoring: Any robot-part or car-to-car contact with a protected running car makes the entire trial score 0, even if it later completes. Red is protected from the start; each returned car becomes protected on its first independent powered motion after complete release and remains protected if it stops. Normal wheel/road and guide/slot contacts are excluded. Otherwise award 0.5 per car that was released by its assigned gripper (yellow: left; blue: right), travels at least 100 mm unassisted clockwise on the powered lane, and remains engaged at the endpoint. The latest robot contact before independent motion must be exclusively the assigned arm and include a fingertip. Wrong-arm or mixed-arm release does not earn that car credit. No eligible cars: 0; one: 0.5; both: 1.0. Loss of lane engagement revokes that car credit. There is no lap, time or parking-pose bonus. A failed native measurement invalidates the run rather than awarding a score.
run_limit: 2400 controls at 20 Hz (120 simulated seconds); Dream evaluation ends at full score or the limit. The scripted feasibility demo continues through release, withdrawal and final observation.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed layout; settle for 0.5 s with red powered, then start the scored trial only with red already running. Off-track cars start approximately 3.5 degrees nose-up, supported by rear tires and the protruding guide. Use seed 0 and no object jitter. Dimensions, exact authored poses and reset validation are in geometry.py/task.py.
fidelity: Native Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim / PhysX. CC0 retained car appearances, with authored chassis, wheels and swivel-guide colliders; nominal mass/friction/inertia and electrical pickup approximation, not a calibrated commercial product. Motors act through wheel joints; contact with the real slot guides the cars. No car pose animation, snap-to-slot or disabled collisions. Low-grip front tires and finite 2 mN m rear-wheel torque are nominal. Electrical braid deformation, material damage and injury are not modeled. Scripted demonstrations use privileged poses and traffic phase and establish feasibility, not learned safety reasoning.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 after 2400 controls; scripted demo: 1.0. The Dream gateway replaced sessions 49 times, so this is not a clean model-performance baseline. Its recorded run predates the assigned-gripper eligibility check; neither car was returned, so its zero is unchanged by that stricter check. The submitted packaged demo validates the final scorer.
